证据说明: Official USENIX Security '25 PDF https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity25-liu-fengyu.pdf downloaded (21-page file including cover; paper pp. 3767-3786) and read through the main text and Appendices A-C; author-hosted mirror https://lfysec.github.io/paper/agentfuzz-security25.pdf also downloaded and confirmed to be the same paper. Identity resolved via the USENIX presentation page (https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/liu-fengyu) and web search: the abstract explicitly names AgentFuzz as the framework. Artifact: GitHub LFYSec/AgentFuzz and Zenodo record 15590097 (files restricted). No arXiv version located under either the official or queue title; queue venue 'ArXiv' is wrong (USENIX Security 2025). Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex API calls were rate-limited (HTTP 429) during this pass, but were not needed once the publisher PDF was obtained. Counts are internally inconsistent (23 vs 27 CVEs).
Memo: [Full-text: full — official USENIX Security 2025 PDF (pp. 3767–3786, 20 pp. plus cover) read through §10 Conclusion, including §7 evaluation, §9 Discussion/Future Work and Appendices A–C.] The queue title is a paraphrase of the paper abstract's sentence 'called AgentFuzz, the first fuzzing framework for detecting taint-style vulnerabilities in LLM-based agents'; the primary record is Liu et al., 'Make Agent Defeat Agent: Automatic Detection of Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in LLM-based Agents', USENIX Security 2025 (https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity25-liu-fengyu.pdf), so the earlier conclusion that it was a distinct paper was incorrect. AgentFuzz is a directed greybox fuzzer for Python LLM-agent web applications with three phases: LLM-assisted seed-prompt generation from CodeQL sink call chains, feedback-driven scheduling (LLM semantic score, CFG distance, penalty), and functionality/argument mutators (self-improvement plus concolic execution with Z3 and longest-common-substring prompt-to-argument mapping). On 20 open-source agents (828 sink callsites, GPT-4o) it reports 34 0-day taint-style vulnerabilities (code/command injection, SQL injection, SSRF, SSTI) at 100% precision and 97.14% recall versus LLMSmith's 2.92% precision and 28.57% recall, with 69.01 CPU hours, 121.8 min average time-to-exposure and 0.69M tokens per agent; all 34 were manually confirmed exploitable (14 required LLM escape, 5 code escape). The contribution secures LLM-agent application services, not an OS kernel, driver or filesystem, so it is adjacent OS-security evidence (Relevance 2) whose fuzzing and LLM-seed-generation methodology plausibly transfers to OS user-space services. Author-stated limits: only single-prompt taint-style bugs, second-order bugs missed (1 of 83 sampled non-vulnerable callsites was truly vulnerable), strict sanitizers defeat constraint solving, and each agent needs manual instrumentation. Internal inconsistency: abstract, conclusion and Table 1 report 23 CVEs, while §7.3 reports 27 CVE identifiers received.
